entry.title: Bitcoin Core security policy update
entry.summary:
Security vulnerabilities have become increasingly easier to identify, especially with advancements in large language models (LLMs) that lower the barrier for discovering certain types of issues and detecting covert fixes. This trend has resulted in a noticeable rise in reported vulnerabilities, prompting a reconsideration of existing security policies.
A central challenge in establishing a security policy is balancing transparency with the need to provide users adequate time to upgrade. While transparency ensures that defenders and attackers have equal access to information, it risks exposing vulnerabilities before users have updated their systems. Traditionally, due to the project’s characteristics and a culture of slow upgrades, the approach favored longer embargo periods, withholding full disclosure and backports until the next major release. However, this method proves ineffective for vulnerabilities that are easily uncovered, as prolonged embargoes do little to protect users and instead postpone the rollout of critical fixes.
To address these concerns, the policy is being revised to distinguish between vulnerabilities based on their discoverability. Vulnerabilities deemed easy to discover—such as those identifiable through straightforward prompts to an LLM—will be flagged during triage. For such cases, fixes will be backported to all actively maintained releases, with prompt releases issued to ensure swift user protection. Details about these vulnerabilities and their resolutions will be published in security advisories alongside the fixed releases.
Further information on the updated security policy can be found at [Bitcoin Core Security Advisories](https://bitcoincore.org/en/security-advisories).
